correctness.rationale: Let \(c\) be the number of orbits of the transitive isometry group on unordered distinct pairs, and let \(s\) be the number of those orbital graphs with valency one. Regularity gives \(2m-1=\sum d_i\ge2c-s\). Each valency-one orbital is an invariant perfect matching whose mate map is a fixed-point-free involution in the centralizer. The centralizer of a transitive action is semiregular, hence its order divides \(2m\); since \(m\) is odd, its Sylow \(2\)-subgroups have order at most two, so it has at most \(m\) involutions. Thus \(s\le m\), \(c\le(3m-1)/2\), and \(\delta(X)\le(3m+1)/2\). The published construction \(D_m\) attains this value for every odd \(m\).
correctness.risk: The proof settles exactly the one-factor-of-two family; it does not address orders with \(2\)-adic valuation at least two.

final_claim: For every odd positive integer \(m\), the maximum number of distances in a \(1\)-homogeneous metric space on \(2m\) points is \((3m+1)/2\), equivalently \(\Delta_1(4k+2)=3k+2\) for every \(k\ge0\).
